description: We love doing what we enjoy.
summary:
SPHEREx Sky Flipbook is a browser-based tool for finding objects that move or change brightness in images from NASA’s SPHEREx mission. Users add SPHEREx FITS images of a patch of sky, or enter its coordinates (RA and Dec), and the tool aligns every exposure north-up and plays them in time order like a short video. Background stars hold still, while nearby stars, brown dwarfs, asteroids, or a possible Planet X shift between frames.

Users can subtract or add epochs, stack exposures by detector band, change the field of view, and overlay Gaia DR3 and AllWISE sources. Clicking any source produces four charts from the loaded data: a spectral energy distribution, a colour–colour diagram, a motion track with proper-motion and parallax fits, and a light curve. A second mode reads user tables (CSV, TSV, JSON, FITS) to detect spectral features such as water ice, CO₂ and methane, and to score moving candidates across two epochs.

SPHEREx images more than a billion objects, far more than any team can inspect alone. Because everything runs in the browser with no installation, anyone can help search that data.
details:
SPHEREx Sky Flipbook is a public web tool for spotting objects that move or change brightness in images from NASA’s SPHEREx mission. A user enters a sky position (RA and Dec) or adds their own SPHEREx FITS images, and the tool aligns every exposure north-up and plays them in time order like a short video. Fixed stars hold still, while movers such as nearby stars, brown dwarfs, asteroids, or a hypothetical Planet X shift between frames.

We built the tool that lets users subtract or add epochs, stack exposures by detector band, choose the field of view, overlay Gaia DR3 and AllWISE sources, view pixel flags, and build a 0.75–5 µm spectrum for any clicked source. A second mode reads user-supplied tables (CSV, TSV, JSON, FITS) to plot spectra with automatic detection of features such as water ice, CO₂ and methane, and to map source positions across two epochs with a candidate score for distant movers.

SPHEREx images more than a billion objects, far more than any one team can inspect. Running entirely in the browser, the tool lets anyone help search that data.
